title: Static Electricity and Circuits
seo_title: Grade 8 Natural Sciences: Static Electricity and Circuits Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 8 Natural Sciences: Static electricity; energy transfer in electrical systems; series and parallel circuits
standard_text: Objects become charged by friction; like charges repel, unlike charges attract. Electric circuits transfer energy from cells to components; current, potential difference and resistance; series and parallel circuits. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 8, Energy and Change: Static electricity; energy transfer in electrical systems; series and parallel circuits)

key_big: Like charges repel; unlike charges attract.
key_sub: Series: one path. Parallel: more than one path.
body_html:
How to think about it

Rubbing two materials together transfers electrons: the one that gains electrons becomes negative, the one that loses them becomes positive. Like charges repel and unlike charges attract. Lightning is a huge discharge of static electricity.

In a circuit, a cell transfers energy to components such as bulbs and resistors. In a series circuit there is one path; adding bulbs makes each dimmer, and if one breaks they all go out. In a parallel circuit each bulb has its own path, so the bulbs stay bright and work separately.

Example

A rubbed balloon sticks to a wall. Why?

Charged objects attract neutral ones.

Answer: it is charged and attracts the wall

Example

Why are house lights wired in parallel?

Each light works alone.

Answer: each can be switched on and off by itself

Common mistakes

  • Thinking positive charges move when rubbing.
  • Thinking current is used up in a circuit.
  • Thinking bulbs in parallel are dimmer.

items.q:
Circuit A
Circuit B
Circuit A has 2 batteries and 2 bulbs in series. Circuit B has 3 batteries and 2 bulbs in series. All the batteries and bulbs are the same. In which circuit is each bulb brighter?
items.e: More batteries in series make bulbs brighter. Bulbs in series share and are dimmer; each bulb in parallel is as bright as one bulb alone.
